price_today.value: $209.00 at the Jackery US store (compare-at $249.00, in stock). Amazon price not read: Amazon blocked the seller check, so there is no confirmed Amazon link to price.

wins.need: Charging laptops, phones and camera gear over USB-C, carried on foot
wins.claim: Beats Jackery's own Explorer 300 (new version) on weight, price and USB-C power. Arithmetic: it is 2.0 lb lighter and $80 cheaper at Jackery's store today. It has two 140 W USB-C ports and one 65 W port. The Explorer 300 has one 100 W USB-C PD port.
wins.figure: 300D: 5.5 lb, $209, USB-C 140 W + 140 W + 65 W. Explorer 300: 7.5 lb, $289, 1 × 100 W USB-C (both from Jackery's US store)
wins.who: Jackery US store (both product listings read the same day, including https://www.jackery.com/products/explorer-300-portable-power-station); port ratings from Jackery FAQ https://faq.jackery.com/hc/en-us/articles/52303653927835-Explorer-300D-Basic-Information

wins.need: Real usable energy, not just the label
wins.claim: A named tester measured 267 Wh delivered from the 288 Wh rated battery, about 93%. Arithmetic: 267 Wh ÷ 5.5 lb = 48.5 delivered Wh per lb. The Explorer 300's rated (not measured) figure is 292 Wh ÷ 7.5 lb = 38.9 Wh/lb.

wins.need: Silent overnight use in a tent or bedroom
wins.claim: No fan. Jackery lists the model as fanless. Best Batteries says the silence held up in use, including under sustained load. Noise was not measured in dB.
wins.figure: Fanless (maker); silence confirmed under sustained load (Best Batteries, no dB figure)
wins.who: Jackery FAQ; Christophe Delpuech, Best Batteries (https://en.best-batteries.com/power-stations/jackery-explorer-300d/)

wins.claim: LiFePO4 rated for 4,000 cycles to 70% capacity. This matches the Explorer 300 rather than beating it, so it is a tie with Jackery's own model and not a win over it.

weak.claim: No AC outlet at all, so it cannot run anything with a wall plug (CPAP on AC, mini fridge, small appliances). AC output is listed as not supported.
Single USB-C recharge input capped at 140 W. Anker's SOLIX C300 DC takes dual USB-C input at 280 W total for full-speed charging.
weak.figure: 300D USB-C input 5–28 V, 140 W max vs Anker C300 DC 280 W total over two ports

weak.claim: Solar is limited to one panel at 100 W max. Solar and car charging cannot run together, nor can wall and solar. 24 V car charging is not supported.
weak.figure: Solar 16–28 V, 6 A, 100 W max, one panel; car input 11–16 V, 96 W max

weak.claim: Jackery's own SolarSaga 100 Air panel ($299) is stated as not compatible with the 300D for recharging.
weak.figure: 'Not compatible with Explorer 300 v2, Explorer 300, 300D, or 240D for recharging.'

weak.claim: No wall charger in the box. The box has the manual and the strap, which doubles as a 140 W USB-C charging cable. Wall charging needs your own USB-C PD charger.
weak.figure: Box: user manual + charging cable/handle strap

weak.claim: No app, no battery expansion, no parallel operation, no water or dust rating.

wins_for: Laptop, phone, camera and drone charging away from outlets, carried in a backpack: two 140 W USB-C ports at 5.5 lb (Jackery store, FAQ)
Jackery shoppers who want the cheapest, lightest Jackery for USB-C and 12 V gear: $209 vs $289 for the Explorer 300 (Jackery store, 2026-11-15)
Silent overnight USB/12 V loads in a tent: fanless (Jackery FAQ; Best Batteries)
Starlink Mini on USB-C at camp, a use Jackery markets the 300D for (maker claim of about 10 hours, not independently measured)
not_for: Anything needing an AC outlet (CPAP on AC, small appliances, mini fridge): the Jackery Explorer 300 with two AC outlets ($289, Jackery store, 2026-11-15) wins instead

Home backup or power outages: 288 Wh with no AC is far too small; a home-backup unit such as the Jackery Explorer 2000 v2 (2042 Wh, 2200 W AC, $999 on Jackery's store 2026-11-15, on pre-order) fits instead
Fastest wall recharge: a dual-USB-C-input station such as the Anker SOLIX C300 DC (280 W total input per Anker) wins on paper, but it is sold out on Anker's US page
Anyone wanting more than 100 W of solar, or Jackery's SolarSaga 100 Air panel: not supported

rivals.where_it_beats_ours: Two AC outlets and 300 W rated output, plus a 120 W car port, so it runs AC devices the 300D cannot. Jackery lists a 5-year warranty on the store page.

rivals.price: Not read: EcoFlow's store returned HTTP 429 on the variant page. The series listing showed $109 but didn't say which capacity (https://us.ecoflow.com/products/trail-series, 2026-11-15).
rivals.where_it_beats_ours: The Solar Lab measured idle drain at about 2 Wh per 24 h, switched on with no load. No equivalent 300D figure exists. The same review describes charging through both two-way 140 W USB-C ports, which the 300D's single 140 W input can't match (https://www.thesolarlab.com/review/ecoflow-trail-300dc, read 2026-11-15).

rivals.price: Sold out on Anker's US page, price not shown (https://www.ankersolix.com/products/c300-dc, read 2026-11-15)
rivals.where_it_beats_ours: Dual PD 3.1 USB-C input at 280 W total for full-speed recharge, against the 300D's 140 W single input (maker page).

targets.headline: Which Jackery should you buy? The lightest one is for laptops, not appliances
targets.why_it_wins_there: It is Jackery's lightest and cheapest answer for USB-C gear: 5.5 lb and $209 vs 7.5 lb and $289 for the Explorer 300, with two 140 W USB-C ports (Jackery US store and FAQ, read 2026-11-15). Best Batteries measured 267 Wh delivered (Christophe Delpuech). The page must say it has no AC.

targets.headline: Jackery portable power stations: do you need wall outlets, or just USB-C?
targets.why_it_wins_there: Same split: the 300D wins for USB-C and 12 V loads on weight and price, and the Explorer 300 wins when an AC outlet is needed (Jackery US store, read 2026-11-15).

targets.headline: A silent backpack battery for phones, laptops and lights at camp
targets.why_it_wins_there: Narrow fit only: fanless (Jackery FAQ; Best Batteries), 5.5 lb, 100 W solar input with about 3.5 h on a SolarSaga 100 (Jackery FAQ). It loses for campers who need AC, so feature it as the no-AC pick, not the overall winner.

record.name: Jackery Explorer 300D Portable Power Station (288 Wh, 2 × 140 W USB-C, no AC)
specs: USB-A 15 W; 12 V 10 A car port
USB-C in 140 W max; solar 16–28 V, 100 W max (one panel); car 11–16 V, 96 W max (about 3.03 h)

record.summary: A 5.5 lb, 288 Wh LiFePO4 battery with two 140 W USB-C ports, a 65 W USB-C port and a 12 V socket, but no AC outlet. Best Batteries measured 267 Wh delivered.
record.fit: People who power laptops, phones, cameras, lights or a Starlink Mini over USB-C or 12 V and carry it by hand or in a pack.
caveats: Recharges through one 140 W USB-C input; no wall charger in the box (Jackery FAQ)
Solar capped at one 100 W panel; Jackery's SolarSaga 100 Air is not compatible (Jackery FAQ; Jackery store)
No app, no expansion battery (Jackery FAQ)
